newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee may continue to be overvalued - NatWest.
newsitem.headline: India rupee may continue to be overvalued - NatWest.

text.p: The Indian rupee may continue to be slightly overvalued in the long-term to aid India's policy objective of encouraging imports and capital inflows, NatWest Securities said on Monday.
India's Finance Ministry has made ambitious capital inflow projections for the Ninth Plan (1997-2002), NatWest said.
"As these materialise into policy actions (fiscal incentives), the current account deficit is expected to widen," it added.

"The Ninth Plan targets an increase in the current account deficit from the current level of 1.74 percent of GDP in 1996/97 (April-March) to an average of 2.4 percent," NatWest Securities said in its report on the Indian rupee.
"This could keep the rupee slightly overvalued in the long term, as that would encourage both imports and capital flows."
The rupee was steady at 35.88/89 against the dollar on Monday.
